text:
Muscle lactate production increases when glycolytic flux exceeds mitochondrial pyruvate oxidation capacity, such as during high-intensity exercise, hypoxia/ischemia, or impaired mitochondrial function, forcing pyruvate conversion to lactate via LDH to regenerate NAD+. Neither listed option is correct: pyruvate is readily formed from glucose breakdown, and oxygen availability would favor pyruvate oxidation rather than lactate production.  
CONFIDENCE: 90
